initiative.title: Agent Runtime v0.8 Adoption and Enforcement
initiative.summary: Make Agent Runtime safely adoptable by existing repositories, mechanically enforce its core lifecycle, and prove the release in Bean Wiki, Allimbot, and Autofolio.

taskset.summary: Deliver brownfield profiles, lifecycle truth, consumer-complete assets, continuity hooks, knowledge and model-economy enforcement, then validate two pilots and one upgrade rehearsal.

tasks.title: Restore lifecycle truth and Work CLI producer-consumer parity
tasks.goal: Make registered work executable and make implemented-but-unclaimed work visible without fabricating history.
tasks.scope: Fix task registration/verification metadata parity, add an honest recovery representation for legacy missing-claim work, and make state reconciliation block projection drift.
acceptance: A task produced by work.py new can be verified and closed without manual frontmatter repair.
State reconciliation detects task, unit, claim, pointer, board, branch, and verification contradictions.
Missing historical claims are represented as explicit recovery evidence and never synthesized as if W2 occurred.
Unknown historical cost or duration is representable without writing a misleading zero.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_work_registration.py tests/test_work_verify.py tests/test_work_close.py tests/test_state_sync_gate.py -q

units.title: Align work registration output with verify and close consumers
units.context: TASK-AR-631 exposed that work.py new renders acceptance and verification only in task body text while work.py verify consumes frontmatter. The same registered task therefore cannot use the advertised lifecycle without manual repair.
units.scope: Persist executable acceptance/verification metadata at registration, preserve legacy body fallback, and add regression coverage. Do not redesign the full work schema.
steps: Add a failing registration-to-verify round-trip test.
Persist task acceptance and verification lists in frontmatter.
Add a safe legacy body fallback for existing tasks.
Prove closeout accepts real evidence and an explicit unavailable-measurement reason.
acceptance: New task frontmatter contains acceptance and verification.
Legacy tasks with valid body verification remain executable.
Unsupported commands fail visibly rather than being silently skipped.
Historical unknown metrics are not coerced to zero.
units.handoff: Report the failing-before/passing-after round trip and the compatibility behavior for existing task records.
units.stop_condition: Stop if the fix requires changing work-item identity or rewriting historical completed records.

units.title: Block task-claim-projection split-brain and support explicit recovery
units.context: The current checkout had an implementation commit and passed unit verification while task/unit/pointer/claim surfaces disagreed. Existing state_sync_gate passed because it did not correlate these sources.
units.scope: Correlate active/implemented work with task, unit, claim, verification, branch, and pointer state; define a loud recovery marker for pre-existing missing-claim history. Do not retroactively create claims.
steps: Add fixtures for the TASK-AR-631 contradiction.
Define blocking findings for impossible active and completed combinations.
Define an explicit recovered-without-claim record shape and reason.
Wire the reconciliation result into the governance chain.
acceptance: The pre-fix TASK-AR-631 shape blocks.
A correctly claimed active task passes.
An explicitly recovered historical task passes with a visible watch signal.
Pointer and UI projections cannot claim no open work while a tracked implementation is in flight.
units.handoff: Provide the contradiction matrix, recovery schema, and governance-chain result.
units.stop_condition: Stop before inventing a generic event-sourcing migration or mutating completed historical claims.

tasks.title: Introduce profile and ownership-aware host configuration
tasks.goal: Represent shared capabilities and host ownership without requiring a project-specific fork of the runtime.
tasks.scope: Add config schema v2 with composable profiles, capabilities, host context, role overlay, state adapters, risk paths, and file ownership modes while preserving v1 config compatibility.
acceptance: Existing v1 agent_runtime.yml files still parse.
Profiles can select core, web-content, security-service, and full-runtime capabilities.
Files can be classified as managed, seed_once, host_owned, or generated.
HOST-CONTEXT and host role/risk/state mappings are machine-consumed.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_doctor.py tests/test_project_context_overlay.py tests/test_host_context_read_location.py tests/test_inventory_sync_sanitize.py -q

units.title: Add backward-compatible profile and ownership config schema
units.context: AgentRuntimeConfig currently exposes only project, upstream, sync mode, overwrite policy, and exact unmanaged paths. That cannot express the Autofolio three-layer model without permanent seams.
units.scope: Implement parsing, validation, defaults, and doctor reporting for config v2. Do not implement sync application in this unit.
steps: Define typed profile, capability, ownership, and host-adapter fields.
Parse v1 and v2 deterministically without a new YAML dependency.
Validate incompatible or unknown profile combinations.
Expose effective configuration through doctor JSON.
acceptance: v1 fixtures remain green.
v2 profile composition is deterministic.
Invalid ownership overlap is a blocker.
Host context has one canonical path.
units.handoff: Document the v1-to-v2 compatibility table and effective config JSON.
units.stop_condition: Stop before mutating a real host or introducing product-specific paths into core defaults.

tasks.title: Build brownfield adopt planning and generated-tree filtering
tasks.goal: Let an existing repository understand exactly what Agent Runtime would add, own, preserve, or conflict with before any mutation.
tasks.scope: Add adopt --plan, pre-adoption doctor mode, generated-directory filtering, host asset detection, and a machine-readable ownership/conflict report.
acceptance: Bean Wiki and Allimbot inventory excludes generated and ignored trees.
Existing AGENTS, Claude agents, skills, and product docs are detected as host assets.
adopt --plan is read-only and reports planned writes and conflicts.
doctor distinguishes pre-adoption readiness from broken installation.

units.title: Implement read-only brownfield adoption planner
units.context: Current inventory produced thousands of review entries for Bean Wiki and Allimbot because generated trees were treated as source, while doctor reported installation absence as nineteen blockers instead of an adoption plan.
inputs: Bean Wiki and Allimbot preflight counts
units.scope: Produce a deterministic, read-only adoption plan and filter generated/ignored content. Do not apply changes in this unit.
steps: Add generated and VCS-ignore aware inventory filtering.
Classify existing host harness assets.
Compute effective profile file set and ownership actions.
Expose text and JSON adopt plans plus pre-adoption doctor mode.
acceptance: Plan output is stable across repeated runs.
Generated dependency/build trees do not appear as host conflicts.
No file is written during adopt --plan.
Every proposed mutation names ownership and reason.
units.handoff: Attach Bean Wiki and Allimbot before/after inventory counts and sample ownership plans.
units.stop_condition: Stop before adopt --apply or host file modification.

tasks.title: Make sync ownership-aware and explicitly reconcilable
tasks.goal: Update safe runtime files without overwriting host state or allowing one expected seam to freeze every unrelated update.
tasks.scope: Apply profile-selected manifests and ownership modes, provide a non-mutating reconcile report, and permit explicit safe-only application without silent merge.
acceptance: seed_once files stop being managed after installation.
host_owned and generated files are never overwritten.
Safe managed updates can be selected explicitly while conflicts remain reported.
Pinned upstream ref, not the locally installed template version, drives comparison.

units.title: Implement ownership manifest and sync reconcile
units.context: Autofolio must list host state and overlays as unmanaged, and one conflict causes the current sync apply to perform zero updates. Exact unmanaged paths cannot scale across heterogeneous hosts.
units.scope: Implement ownership-aware planning, reconcile output, and explicit safe-only application. Do not auto-merge host edits.
steps: Build the effective manifest from profile and ownership config.
Separate managed updates, seeds, host-owned files, generated views, and conflicts.
Add reconcile JSON and an explicit safe-only apply mode.
Lock the installed ownership manifest and pinned ref.
acceptance: No host-owned or generated file enters an apply set.
Safe-only apply is opt-in and reports skipped conflicts.
No silent overwrite path is introduced.
Legacy unmanaged config still behaves compatibly.
units.handoff: Provide manifest examples for core, web-content, security-service, and Autofolio upgrade.
units.stop_condition: Stop before implementing automatic three-way merges.

tasks.title: Enforce consumer template and skill dependency closure
tasks.goal: Guarantee that every capability advertised to a clean host has all executable dependencies in the selected profile.
tasks.scope: Add a dependency-closure gate, ship or rewire missing work/release/session helpers, and expand clean-host smoke to exercise declared skills.
acceptance: Every shipped SKILL dependency exists in its effective profile.
work.py and required helpers execute in a clean installed host.
Template smoke exercises work status/new/verify and session closeout dependencies.
Profile reduction never leaves dangling docs or hook commands.

units.title: Add profile-aware asset dependency closure and clean-host lifecycle smoke
units.context: The host template advertises independent-verification, work-analytics, release-conductor, and session-closeout skills while omitting several scripts they require.
units.scope: Close declared dependency gaps and run a clean-host lifecycle smoke. Do not copy unrelated root-only development assets into every profile.
steps: Parse skill and hook dependencies from the selected manifest.
Fail on absent or cross-profile dangling dependencies.
Ship package entrypoints or thin wrappers for required lifecycle commands.
Exercise them from an installed wheel fixture.
acceptance: The previously missing work, release, session, and save-report dependencies are resolved or removed from advertised profiles.
A clean host completes status, registration, verification, and closeout smoke.
Dotfiles and executable wrappers are present in the wheel.
units.handoff: Report dependency counts per profile and clean-host command results.
units.stop_condition: Stop if closure would require shipping a product-specific role or path in core.

tasks.title: Provide cross-platform start, compact, and resume continuity hooks
tasks.goal: Make the harness actually enter and re-enter its governance path on supported agent clients and operating systems.
tasks.scope: Replace Windows-only hook commands, add hook installation/doctor checks, and checkpoint/rebootstrap around compaction and interrupted sessions.
acceptance: Linux and Windows hook command paths execute.
SessionStart runs host context, active work, compound lookup, and resume checks.
PreCompact checkpoints and PostCompact rebootstrap are installed where supported.
Missing or stale hooks are visible in doctor.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_bootstrap_dev_env.py tests/test_session_resume_check.py tests/test_interrupted_run_detector.py tests/test_doctor.py tests/test_template_smoke.py -q

units.title: Replace platform-specific hook shims with verified Python entrypoints
units.context: The shipped Codex hooks invoke .cmd files for update, prompt, governance, and Allimbot actions. The existing session_start_hook is not wired into those hooks, reproducing the Tag Manual dogfooding bypass.
units.scope: Use portable Python commands and client-supported platform overrides, add compact checkpoint/rebootstrap, and verify hook presence. Do not assume unsupported hook events without capability detection.
steps: Define portable hook entrypoints.
Wire SessionStart and supported compact events.
Add commandWindows only where necessary.
Teach doctor to validate effective hooks and dependencies.
acceptance: No POSIX path depends on a .cmd file.
Hook commands resolve in a clean host.
Compaction capability degrades explicitly when unsupported.
Session resume finds active or recovered work.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_bootstrap_dev_env.py tests/test_session_resume_check.py tests/test_doctor.py tests/test_template_smoke.py -q
units.handoff: Provide the client/OS hook matrix and simulated compact/restart logs.
units.stop_condition: Stop before editing per-user agent settings without explicit Owner action.

tasks.title: Make compound and scribe task-linked and host-configurable
tasks.goal: Prevent repeated mistakes and accumulated context without forcing every host into one monolithic status format.
tasks.scope: Introduce per-entry compound records, task/signature linkage, start/failure lookup, and configurable scribe state adapters with generated summaries.
acceptance: A repeated defect produces a task-linked compound record and a later matching task surfaces it.
Closure accepts only compound/review evidence linked to the current task or defect signature.
Scribe reads host-configured status sources and emits generated projections.
Live host data is seed_once or host_owned, never permanently managed.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_compound_cadence_gate.py tests/test_compound_cadence_obligation.py tests/test_closure_gate.py tests/test_doc_steward_due.py -q

units.title: Introduce per-entry task-linked compound records and retrieval
units.context: Current closure can be satisfied by any same-day compound/review/retro and the template ships a managed monolithic compound_log placeholder that collides with host data.
units.scope: Create and query individual compound records keyed by work ID and defect signature; generate indexes. Do not migrate every historical compound entry in this unit.
steps: Define compound record schema and deterministic signature.
Add task-start and post-failure lookup.
Require linked evidence for repeat-defect closeout.
Generate a conflict-free index.
acceptance: Unrelated same-day records do not satisfy closeout.
A matching signature is surfaced before implementation.
Concurrent compounds do not edit one shared data file.
units.handoff: Provide a repeat-defect fixture showing create, retrieve, and closeout enforcement.
units.stop_condition: Stop before bulk-rewriting historical compound logs.

units.title: Add configurable scribe state adapters and generated projections
units.context: scribe_due assumes a lead-engineer STATUS file and one Korean heading, so Bean Wiki BACKLOG and Allimbot PROJECT_STATUS cannot participate reliably.
inputs: Bean Wiki BACKLOG and Allimbot PROJECT_STATUS conventions
units.scope: Read configured host state sources, compute scribe due status, and emit generated summaries without taking ownership of host canonical files.
steps: Define state source and projection config.
Support structured and markdown adapters.
Report due/block policy by work size.
Test Bean Wiki and Allimbot fixture layouts.
acceptance: No exact Korean heading is required.
Missing optional host status degrades visibly.
Substantial closeout can enforce overdue scribe while mini tasks remain lightweight.
units.handoff: Provide adapter examples for runtime, Bean Wiki, Allimbot, and Autofolio.
units.stop_condition: Stop before changing host status files during read-only doctor or session start.

tasks.title: Make model routing economically effective and auditable
tasks.goal: Use lower-cost native subagents by default where appropriate and prove when escalation actually changed the invoked model.
tasks.scope: Detect provider capabilities, distinguish advisory from enforced routing, record dispatch justification and actual usage, and block false cost-saving claims.
acceptance: Equivalent tier mappings are reported as ineffective.
Every subagent dispatch records reason, requested tier, resolved model, escalation signal, and actual usage when available.
Deterministic tools run before model delegation.
Runtime uses native provider agents rather than rebuilding an executor.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_model_routing.py tests/test_role_routing.py tests/test_role_routing_wiring.py tests/test_provider_import_contract.py -q

units.title: Add effective-tier detection and dispatch cost ledger
units.context: Codex haiku, sonnet, and opus tiers currently resolve to the same default model, so the policy records different labels without reducing token cost.
units.scope: Resolve configured provider models, flag ineffective tiers, and append dispatch/usage records. Do not embed provider credentials or implement a separate agent executor.
steps: Detect effective tier-to-model equivalence.
Add routing status to doctor.
Record dispatch decision and escalation reason.
Ingest actual token/cost/latency when the provider exposes it.
acceptance: Same-model tiers cannot be reported as savings.
Low-cost routing is the default for worker-ready routine units.
Critical or failed work records a visible escalation.
Missing usage telemetry is marked unverified, not zero.
units.handoff: Provide routing matrices for Claude and Codex plus sample dispatch ledger records.
units.stop_condition: Stop before hardcoding an unverified current model catalog or storing API secrets.

tasks.title: Adopt native Allimbot events and security-service guardrails
tasks.goal: Use current durable, allowlisted Allimbot delivery and add reusable security/external-effect controls for service hosts.
tasks.scope: Replace the legacy runtime notifier with ProjectEmitter-compatible events, add the security-service profile, and preserve fail-open delivery without secret leakage.
acceptance: Runtime emits only allowlisted current Allimbot events.
Delivery uses v1/events and durable spool behavior.
Allimbot unavailability never blocks local work.
Security-service profile covers secrets, auth, migration, and production external effects.

units.title: Replace legacy notifier with optional native ProjectEmitter adapter
units.context: The template still targets 127.0.0.1:8787/trigger and can post directly to ntfy, while current Allimbot uses allowlisted project recipes, ALLIMBOT_ENDPOINT, project tokens, v1/events, and a durable spool.
units.scope: Use Allimbot as an optional dependency or compatible adapter, enforce recipe allowlists, and add security profile mappings. Do not introduce a mandatory circular dependency.
steps: Define the runtime event boundary.
Use ProjectEmitter when installed and a compatible local spool adapter otherwise.
Remove implicit direct-ntfy delivery from standard mode.
Add redaction, allowlist, and fail-open tests.
acceptance: Legacy /trigger is absent from standard mode.
Unknown event types and metadata are rejected locally.
No token, prompt, or secret enters event data.
Offline events remain recoverable.
units.handoff: Provide event compatibility and security matrices against the current Allimbot recipe.
units.stop_condition: Stop before changing Allimbot production credentials or sending live external notifications.

tasks.title: Run the Bean Wiki web-content pilot
tasks.goal: Prove lightweight adoption preserves the existing editorial harness while adding task trace, compound, scribe, and model economy.
tasks.scope: Use a clean Bean Wiki worktree, apply core plus web-content profile, run three non-publishing tasks, and capture adoption and runtime evidence.
acceptance: Existing AGENTS, editorial agents, skills, and content rules are unchanged except an explicit runtime include/adapter.
Three real tasks complete with trace and no claimless diff.
One compound retrieval and one restart/compaction recovery are demonstrated.
No live content publish occurs.

units.title: Adopt and exercise core plus web-content in Bean Wiki
units.context: Bean Wiki has strong host-owned editorial agents and publishing gates but no common task/claim/compound/scribe/model-cost harness.
units.scope: Run adoption plan/apply in a clean host worktree, preserve editorial assets, execute three safe tasks, and collect evidence. No push, deploy, or live publish.
steps: Capture pre-adoption state and ownership plan.
Apply core plus web-content profile.
Run mini-task, specialist review, and restart scenarios.
Run Bean content/editorial gates and record metrics.
acceptance: Unexpected host overwrite count is zero.
Doctor blockers and dangling dependencies are zero.
Task trace is complete for all pilot diffs.
All publish commands remain dry-run or uncalled.
units.handoff: Attach before/after inventory, adoption duration, seams, task trace, model routing, and Bean verification output.
units.stop_condition: Stop before live publish, origin push, or modification of unrelated dirty host work.

tasks.title: Run the Allimbot security-service pilot
tasks.goal: Prove runtime adoption works in a mixed Python/Next/Supabase security-sensitive service and uses native Allimbot events.
tasks.scope: Use a clean Allimbot worktree, apply core plus security-service, complete ordinary and critical tasks plus offline event recovery, and keep production external effects blocked.
acceptance: Existing product security and release policies remain host-owned.
An ordinary task and a Critical task both complete with correct review routing.
Offline native events spool and recover without secret leakage.
No production deployment or credential change occurs.

units.title: Adopt and exercise core plus security-service in Allimbot
units.context: Allimbot already has mature product security and durable event integration but no common development-process task/claim/compound/scribe/model-cost harness.
units.scope: Run profile adoption and three pilot scenarios in a clean worktree with production effects disabled.
steps: Capture host context, risk paths, and verification commands.
Apply core plus security-service profile.
Run ordinary, Critical, and offline-event tasks.
Run Python/web/security gates and record results.
acceptance: Unexpected host overwrite count is zero.
Critical work requires independent security review.
Event metadata is allowlisted and secret-free.
Production deployment remains blocked.
units.handoff: Attach adoption, test, security-review, event-spool, and external-effect evidence.
units.stop_condition: Stop before production deploy, remote account mutation, secret creation, or modification of the active dirty host branch.

tasks.title: Rehearse Autofolio v0.6 to v0.8 migration
tasks.goal: Prove the new ownership/profile model materially reduces Autofolio's unmanaged seams without changing product behavior.
tasks.scope: Run a clean migration plan and safe apply rehearsal, classify all current seams, and verify product tests without product feature changes.
acceptance: Every current unmanaged path has a managed, seed_once, host_owned, generated, or temporary-conflict disposition.
Temporary seams decrease materially.
No Autofolio product file is silently overwritten.
The v0.6 to RC migration is repeatable from a clean worktree.

units.title: Execute and document the Autofolio migration rehearsal
units.context: Autofolio is pinned to v0.6.0 and uses the right framework/overlay/seam design, but carries 21 unmanaged entries caused by host data, product context, and upstream defects.
units.scope: Rehearse configuration migration and safe sync in a clean Autofolio worktree. Do not implement or alter investment-product behavior.
steps: Snapshot v0.6 ownership and seams.
Generate v0.8 migration and reconcile plans.
Apply only safe managed updates.
Run host verification and quantify remaining seams.
acceptance: Migration is idempotent.
Live host data is not managed.
Every remaining seam has an explicit host-specific reason.
Product tests remain green.
units.handoff: Attach the seam ledger, migration diff, host verification, and rollback instructions.
units.stop_condition: Stop before product feature changes, live trading effects, origin push, or main-branch mutation.

tasks.title: Prepare v0.8.0 release candidate from pilot evidence
tasks.goal: Produce an exact, installable v0.8.0-rc.1 candidate whose release claims are backed by clean-host, pilot, migration, and browser evidence.
tasks.scope: Run version/document cascade, tag freshness, clean-tag installs, mandatory browser smoke, release council gates, and prepare but do not publish the final release without Owner approval.
acceptance: README, package, module, template, lock, and release metadata agree on v0.8.0-rc.1.
Tag discovery cannot silently use stale local refs.
Clean installs from the exact candidate tag pass lifecycle and browser smoke.
Bean Wiki, Allimbot, and Autofolio evidence is linked from release readiness.

units.title: Assemble and verify the v0.8.0-rc.1 release candidate
units.context: The current package reports v0.7.0 while README examples still pin v0.1.8, and local tag discovery can use stale refs. The open v0.8 release issue predates the adoption/enforcement pilot evidence.
units.scope: Prepare and verify an RC commit and release plan. Final tag push and GitHub Release remain Owner-gated.
steps: Require fresh remote tag discovery.
Run the version and documentation cascade.
Build and install the exact candidate in clean environments.
Run full, browser, pilot, migration, and release gates.
Produce the Owner approval packet.
acceptance: No stale version or tag reference remains.
All mandatory release evidence is exact-SHA linked.
Skipped browser exploration is not accepted for RC.
No final release is published without explicit Owner approval.
units.handoff: Provide the exact candidate SHA, install commands, evidence matrix, rollback plan, and remaining Owner decision.
units.stop_condition: Stop before final tag push, GitHub Release publication, or closing the release approval issue.
